findings.title: The unconstrained live coding prompt can exhaust its turn budget after proving the full tool path
findings.observation: Two unchanged executions of the broad cross-Gate coding prompt each traversed the gateway, emitted and executed eleven Sandbox-owned tool requests, returned authoritative results, called the model again and cleaned every container, but ended FAILED/BUDGET_EXCEEDED at maxTurns=12.
findings.reproduction: Run `python docs/checkpoints/GATE-3-CP-0006/audit-harness/cross_gate_live.py --report docs/checkpoints/GATE-3-CP-0006/CROSS-GATE-LIVE.json` with the configured provider/model. The preserved first and second command records are cmd-0015 and cmd-0016.
findings.expected: A bounded audit prompt should complete SUCCEEDED after the real tool round-trip it is intended to prove.
findings.observed: Both broad-prompt repetitions reached FAILED/BUDGET_EXCEEDED only after multiple valid end-to-end tool cycles. The separately executed configured-model scenario reached SUCCEEDED with seven Sandbox tool executions, no repair and an APPROVED result, so the required production path itself has positive evidence.
findings.impact: This is audit-scenario nondeterminism and may waste time or provider calls; it does not create host execution, bypass the Sandbox, lose a ToolResult, or leave a run indefinitely RUNNING. Critical and High thresholds remain clear.
findings.recommendedCorrection: In a later implementing checkpoint, make the diagnostic cross-Gate prompt deterministically terminate within its declared turn budget or give the scenario a task-specific completion contract. Preserve the production budgets and do not weaken the requirement that a positive proof end SUCCEEDED.

observations.title: The positive cross-Gate proof is the configured-model run
observations.detail: LIVE-CODING-RUN.json records the configured model, ten gateway calls, seven canonical ToolRequests, seven Sandbox executions, seven authoritative results, a later model call, no host-sentinel change, no surviving container, zero repair attempts and terminal SUCCEEDED/APPROVED. The two budget-exhausted broad-prompt attempts are retained rather than substituted or hidden.

observations.title: The first 19-attack Red Team attempt exposed an audit-reader defect, not an escaped defense
observations.detail: All nineteen mutations were DEFENDED, but the audit reader looked for a nonexistent top-level nullControl field and therefore marked its baseline invalid. RED-TEAM-ATTEMPT-1.json preserves the failed report hash and cause. Only the audit-only reader was corrected, after which the whole battery was required to repeat.
